title: News Digest: Europe Faces Long, Cold Winter as Fuel Buffers Dwindle

html:
Europe is heading into winter with dangerously fragile energy supplies, as conflicts in the Middle East and Russia tighten global markets for liquefied natural gas and heating oil, driving inventories to worryingly low levels.

Gas and heating oil remain Europe’s primary residential heating sources, accounting for roughly 30% and 10% of household demand, respectively. After successive years of energy shocks, the region again faces winter with both markets under severe strain.

Europe’s vulnerability stems largely from its post-2022 energy transformation, when it replaced Russian pipeline gas with LNG following Moscow’s invasion of Ukraine. That shift reduced dependence on Russia but left Europe competing globally for LNG, exposing it to supply disruptions that can ripple through markets almost instantly.

That fragility has become increasingly evident. Europe is falling behind the pace needed to refill LNG inventories before winter, with underground gas storage around 55% full, the lowest for this time of year since 2021, according to LSEG data. LNG imports have also slowed sharply since the Iran conflict began, with July imports on track to total just 6.3 million metric tons, the lowest since September 2024, per Kpler.

Much of the shortfall reflects Asia’s return to the market, with the region drawing a record 4 million tons of U.S. LNG supply in June and July, diverting cargoes that might otherwise have gone to Europe. Hopes that Qatar would restore exports after the Strait of Hormuz briefly reopened following an April U.S.-Iran interim deal have faded, as renewed blockades amid escalating tensions have disrupted flows again.

The combination of low inventories, weak imports and a worsening supply outlook has rattled European markets, pushing benchmark gas prices above €60 per megawatt hour last week, their highest since early 2023. While higher prices may eventually draw more LNG cargoes to Europe, the region appears likely to enter winter with storage levels well below its 80% target.
